<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z ≈ 199 with a strong M+2 peak of similar intensity, indicating a single bromine atom (79 Br/81 Br). Subtracting the bromine mass (79) leaves 120 Da, which corresponds to the formula C₈H₈O. Adding the bromine gives C₈H₈OBr (exact monoisotopic mass 199.0). A common structure matching this formula is bromo‑acetophenone, i.e., a phenyl‑acetyl group bearing a bromine on the aromatic ring. The SMILES for para‑bromo‑acetophenone is **CC(=O)c1ccc(Br)cc1**. This structure is chemically reasonable and fits the observed mass‑spectrometric pattern. 

The task asks for the SMILES string of the organic sample, so the final answer is the SMILES of the identified compound.
